metadata.title: R2: Polarization and Trust
metadata.description: Super PAC money disproportionately funds negative ads, which harden polarization, which produces institutional conflict, public frustration, falling trust, and tribal voting — which deepens polarization further.
metadata.author: US Government Intelligent Textbook

nodes.label: Political Polarization
nodes.description: The ideological and emotional distance between the two major parties and their voters.

nodes.label: Institutional Conflict
nodes.description: Government shutdowns, debt-ceiling brinkmanship, blocked confirmations — visible breakdowns in inter-branch cooperation.

nodes.label: Public Frustration
nodes.description: Citizens' sense of being unheard, exhausted, or alarmed by political dysfunction.

nodes.label: Trust In Government
nodes.description: The percentage of citizens who say they trust the federal government to do what is right.

nodes.label: Cynicism and Tribal Voting
nodes.description: Voting against the other team rather than for one's own. Both parties seen as compromised.

edges.description: Polarized politicians refuse to cooperate, producing gridlock and shutdowns.
Visible government dysfunction exhausts and alarms citizens.
Frustration and anxiety pull trust down.
When trust collapses, voters fall back on team loyalty — voting against the other side rather than for any positive vision.
Tribal voting reinforces the parties' polarized self-images.

loops.label: R2: Polarization and Trust
loops.description: A self-feeding cycle where each turn hardens partisan hostility.
